Forecast Discussion

It’s the coldest morning of the season-to-date, with colder valleys in the upper 20s to lower 30s. Skies are sunny for your Sunday with a more pleasant afternoon, but remaining on the cool side.

The weather pattern over North America is “blocky”, that is, there are significant storm features off both East and West Coasts of the United States. Closer to home, a significant coastal cyclone is developing well east of the Carolina coastline today. Meanwhile, Canadian high pressure is building southward into our area from the Mid-Atlantic.

This is a stable weather map configuration that will hold through much of the workweek. The air mass will modify under the still relatively-strong mid-October sun angle.

By late week, the current high will be replenished by a new high arriving from the Great Lakes region. This will send temperatures down only modestly by the end of the period.

It’s a completely dry week. The question then becomes, will we even have any more meaningful rainfall during the month of October?
